# Homer — Odyssey I (Murray, 1919)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** Homer, *The Odyssey*, vol. 1, trans. A. T. Murray (London: William Heinemann; New York: G. P. Putnam’s Sons, 1919), 8.296–325.

**Shortened note:** Homer, *Odyssey*, 8.296–325.

**Bibliography:** Homer. *The Odyssey*. Vol. 1. Translated by A. T. Murray. London: William Heinemann; New York: G. P. Putnam’s Sons, 1919. https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.01.0136%3Abook%3D8%3Acard%3D295.

## Essay use

Murray’s Homeric translation supplies a narrated capture: Hephaestus’s “bonds” prevent Ares and Aphrodite from escaping, and the poem frames the resulting public scene through shame and laughter. This is provenance for the Offered image in §2/#3.

**Claim boundary:** the passage uses “bonds,” not a general modern theory of surveillance or technological control. It does not mention Harmonia, establish Hesiodic genealogy, or prove the essay’s two-logics reading.

<a id="homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q001"></a>
## Passage card — `homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q001` — Hephaestus’s complaint
^homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q001

> “Father Zeus, and ye other blessed gods that are forever, come hither that ye may see a laughable matter and a monstrous, even how Aphrodite, daughter of Zeus, scorns me for that I am lame and loves destructive Ares because he is comely and strong of limb, whereas I was born misshapen.”

- **Locator:** *Odyssey*, 8.305–310.
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manually transcribed from the line-located Perseus Murray text and reread in the source card; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Argument function:** mythic narrative provenance.
- **Consumers:** [[22-s2-p3-ares-aphrodite-harmonia]]; [Hephaestus and the Net](../../../../../mytheme/worlds/hellenic/ares-aphrodite-hephaestus-poseidon/WHOLE.md); movement 22 Homeric scene.
- **Use boundary:** voices Hephaestus’s complaint within an embedded song; it does not establish a universal theory of war, desire, or justice.

<a id="homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q002` — bonds and capture
^homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q002

> “And about them clung the cunning bonds of the wise Hephaestus, nor could they in any wise stir their limbs or raise them up. Then at length they learned that there was no more escaping.”

- **Locator:** *Odyssey*, 8.296–300.
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manually transcribed from the line-located Perseus Murray text and reread in the source card; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Argument function:** mythic narrative provenance.
- **Consumers:** [[22-s2-p3-ares-aphrodite-harmonia]]; [Hephaestus and the Net](../../../../../mytheme/worlds/hellenic/ares-aphrodite-hephaestus-poseidon/WHOLE.md); [[A23-Trust-Faith-and-the-Formal-Limit|Trust]]; movement 22 capture image.
- **Use boundary:** establishes a specific narrated capture through bonds; it does not justify calling the passage a theory of surveillance, harmony, dialectic, or planetary computation.

<a id="homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q003"></a>
## Passage card — `homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q003` — shame and laughter
^homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q003

> “Now the goddesses abode for shame each in her own house, but the gods, the givers of good things, stood in the gateway; and unquenchable laughter arose among the blessed gods as they saw the craft of wise Hephaestus.”

- **Locator:** *Odyssey*, 8.320–325.
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manually transcribed from the line-located Perseus Murray text and reread in the source card; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** qualifies.
- **Argument function:** counterposition / reception boundary.
- **Consumers:** [[22-s2-p3-ares-aphrodite-harmonia]]; [Hephaestus and the Net](../../../../../mytheme/worlds/hellenic/ares-aphrodite-hephaestus-poseidon/WHOLE.md); [[A23-Trust-Faith-and-the-Formal-Limit|Trust]]; movement 22 offered-reading limitation.
- **Use boundary:** the public response is shame and laughter, not stated concord; it blocks treating the capture itself as an ancient image of harmony.
<a id="homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q004"></a>
## Passage card — `homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q004` — Helios the informer
^homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q004

> "even Helius, who had marked them as they lay together in love." — and, on the return: Helios "kept watch for him and told him the tale" (σκοπιὴν ἔχεν, a lookout-post).

- **Locator:** *Odyssey*, 8.270–71 and 8.302.
- **Status:** wording-verified against the public Murray text (Theoi mirror of the Loeb); reread against the line-located Perseus text pending.
- **Verification:** Coordinator, 2026-07-18; Greek key-term σκοπιή confirmed at 8.302 via DCC Greek text.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Argument function:** the apparatus's detection layer — the sun-god as sensor and informant, twice.
- **Consumers:** [[22-s2-p3-ares-aphrodite-harmonia]]; [[40-s5-p3-preference-hidden-zero]]; [[section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C25-Counterfeit-Gathering]].
- **Use boundary:** narrated surveillance within the song; the technological reading is the essay's Argued development.

<a id="homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q005"></a>
## Passage card — `homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q005` — the artful bonds forged
^homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q005

> Bonds forged on the anvil "which might not be broken or loosed," "fine as spiders' webs, so that no one even of the blessed gods could see them"; when the trap springs they are the "artful bonds" — δεσμοὶ τεχνήεντες — that pour around the lovers.

- **Locator:** *Odyssey*, 8.274–81 (forging; ἀρρήκτους ἀλύτους; ἠύτ᾽ ἀράχνια λεπτά) and 8.296–97 (δεσμοὶ τεχνήεντες).
- **Status:** wording-verified against the public Murray text; Greek terms confirmed via DCC; Perseus reread pending.
- **Verification:** Coordinator, 2026-07-18. The poem's own word for the device is δόλος, snare (8.276, 282).
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Argument function:** technē named on the net itself — the arche-technē anchor in two Homeric words.
- **Consumers:** [[22-s2-p3-ares-aphrodite-harmonia]]; [[section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C25-Counterfeit-Gathering]]; myth history.
- **Use boundary:** the epithet licenses "artful bonds," not a Homeric theory of technology.

<a id="homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q006"></a>
## Passage card — `homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q006` — the account: bride-gifts and the adulterer's fine
^homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q006

> Hephaestus will keep the lovers bound "until her father pays back to me all the gifts of wooing" (ἕεδνα); the anonymous god's gnome closes: "The slow catches the swift; even as now Hephaestus, slow though he is… has out-stripped Ares for all that he is the swiftest of the gods… lame though he is, by craft (τέχνῃσι); and so Ares owes the fine of the adulterer (μοιχάγρια)."

- **Locator:** *Odyssey*, 8.317–20 (ἕεδνα) and 8.329–32 (gnome; μοιχάγρια, a Homeric hapax).
- **Status:** wording-verified against the public Murray text; Perseus reread pending.
- **Verification:** Coordinator, 2026-07-18. Note: the gnome is spoken by an anonymous god glancing at his neighbour (8.328), not by Hephaestus.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Argument function:** relation converted to account — the caring-to-accounting hinge; technē named as the winning power in the gods' own verdict.
- **Consumers:** [[22-s2-p3-ares-aphrodite-harmonia]]; [[40-s5-p3-preference-hidden-zero]]; [[section-rooms/arguments/A23-Trust-Faith-and-the-Formal-Limit|Trust, Faith, and the Formal Limit]].
- **Use boundary:** Greek legal texture (Phillips) carries the institutional claim; this card carries only the narrated demand and fine.

<a id="homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q007"></a>
## Passage card — `homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q007` — Hermes and the price of exposure
^homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q007

> "Would that this might befall, lord Apollo… that thrice as many bonds inextricable might clasp me about, and ye gods, aye, and all the goddesses too might be looking on, but that I might sleep by the side of golden Aphrodite."

- **Locator:** *Odyssey*, 8.334–42.
- **Status:** wording-verified against the public Murray text; Perseus reread pending.
- **Verification:** Coordinator, 2026-07-18.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Argument function:** the incentive economy of the apparatus — total exposure rationally embraced once spectacle is currency; more laughter follows.
- **Consumers:** [[22-s2-p3-ares-aphrodite-harmonia]]; [[40-s5-p3-preference-hidden-zero]].
- **Use boundary:** a joke within the song; the engagement-economy reading is the essay's Argued development.

<a id="homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q008"></a>
## Passage card — `homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q008` — Poseidon's surety and the release
^homer-1919-odyssey-murray-q008

> Poseidon, who does not laugh (8.344), presses: "Loose him; I promise he shall pay all that is right among the immortal gods." Hephaestus: "wretched are the sureties taken for the wretched" (δειλαί τοι δειλῶν γε καὶ ἐγγύαι ἐγγυάασθαι). Poseidon: if Ares flees the debt, "I will myself pay thee this." Then Hephaestus "loosed the bonds, and the two, when they were freed from the bonds, strong though they were, sprang up straightway" — Ares to Thrace, Aphrodite to Paphos, where the Graces bathed and anointed her.

- **Locator:** *Odyssey*, 8.344–58 (ἐγγύη exchange) and 8.359–66 (release and departures).
- **Status:** wording-verified against the public Murray text; Perseus reread pending.
- **Verification:** Coordinator, 2026-07-18.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** supports.
- **Argument function:** the surety closure — the completed apparatus cannot conclude; a person standing-for another at risk of loss ends the scene, accepted by the maker against his own stated distrust of sureties.
- **Consumers:** [[22-s2-p3-ares-aphrodite-harmonia]]; [[40-s5-p3-preference-hidden-zero]]; [[46-s50-p3-4-2-mono-poly]]; [[section-rooms/arguments/A23-Trust-Faith-and-the-Formal-Limit|Trust, Faith, and the Formal Limit]].
- **Use boundary:** the legal-form claim (formal ἐγγύη procedure) is carried by [[symbolon/episteme/sources/classical-philology/phillips/phillips-moicheia-unity-greek-law/phillips-moicheia-unity-greek-law.md|phillips-moicheia-unity-greek-law]]; the analogy to alignment-era trust displacement is the essay's Argued move.
